newsitem.title: UK: Smithkline reined in by stronger pound.
newsitem.headline: Smithkline reined in by stronger pound.

text.p: Drugs giant SmithKline Beecham Plc said Tuesday the surging British pound muffled an otherwise strong rise in first-quarter profits.

Underlining the challenge to British-based companies, the Anglo-U.S. group said the pound's rise against other European currencies and the dollar wiped 41 million pounds ($66 million) off profits in the first three months of the year.
Pre-tax profits rose 8 percent to 418 million pounds ($674 million), while sales actually fell by 2 percent to 1.84 billion pounds ($2.97 billion.)
At constant exchange rates the company said its pre-tax profit would have been ahead by 19 percent.

SmithKline Beecham, which is the world's ninth biggest prescription drugs group in terms of market share, again pointed to a robust performance by products launched over the past five years as a sign of its rude good health.

Sales of new drugs jumped by 40 percent to 354 million pounds ($571 million) in the first quarter, led by rapid growth in Seroxat/Paxil, an anti-depressant rival to Eli Lilly & Co.'s blockbuster Prozac.
Sales of Seroxat/Paxil climbed 49 percent in the three months to March, putting it in a race with antibiotic Augmentin to be the company's biggest seller.
Sales in the consumer healthcare, which includes a string of household names such as Aquafresh toothpaste, Lucozade and Panadol, rose ahead 18 percent and operating profits rose 20 percent.
The company's U.S. Clinical Laboratories operations continued to limp along amid strong competition for its hospital testing services, with profits dropping 25 percent.
